parentStaticReview: Parent reviewed the corrected native full/terminal quartet and accepted the semantic identity and natural tightening on 2026-10-20. This is static phase review, not live animation acceptance.
actualCaveats: This is a nonloop assembly and tightening sequence, not a conserved rigid ring simply translating. Four broken arc segments join into two long arcs, then the secondary lower band and central clasps form; no frame is a global opacity fade.

The first pose includes a short lower-left nascent band strip. It is absent as a separate strip in aligning-ring, then the complete second lower band is present at closure, matching the original four-pose staging rather than proving continuous material correspondence.

The aligning pose has a near/actual alpha128 contact between its upper-left arc and left clasp, while other side gaps remain open. It is partial latching, not four perfectly symmetric open joints. Some thin side gaps and the secondary-band slit are subordinate at native 32 and clearer at 64.

The five peripheral diamond identities persist, but their paths are independently authored and uneven. The upper-right fragment descends from the first to the aligning pose, while the others move less. No constant-speed particle interpolation is claimed.

Main-assembly widths are 915, 905, 891, 791 source pixels. Selected closure-to-terminal contraction is 11.2% in width and 10.0% in height; the rejected first terminal contracted 23.6% in width. This is intentional restraint tightening, not whole-pad motion or per-frame fitting.

Total source alpha mass changes by +39.1%, +26.8%, then -16.8%. The addition of central clasps and a second band makes assembly cadence uneven at 12 fps, even after the excessive terminal shrink was repaired.

Side-clasp diagnostic midlines span x623.25..627.5 and y627.25..641, within 0.095 and 0.307 logical pixels respectively. They support common visual registration but do not imply identical object silhouettes or a fixed physical emitter.

The terminal double ring stays visible. There is no runtime loop, authored blank ending, extra final hold, scene removal time or 420/500 ms lifecycle. APNG encoding and static images are verified; browser and live-game playback remain unobserved.
